Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.

A: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no AbortSignal timeout, so a hung parent sync endpoint stalls the token-refresh path with no bound. Calendar availability and booking operations that need a token refresh block for up to the platform's default idle timeouts (minutes) per call whenever the parent cal.com endpoint is slow or down, turning a remote outage into local request stalls on the booking path.
B: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is issued with no timeout or AbortSignal, yet it sits inline on the request path of every calendar and video operation once the feature is enabled. A hung or slow parent endpoint (mid-deploy restart, network partition) stalls each affected booking/calendar request for up to undici's default multi-minute header/body timeouts instead of failing fast, and concurrent requests pile up against the parent, degrading every booking that touches a synced app.
